name: Liposonix

card.summary: A non-surgical high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) device that heats and disrupts fat beneath the skin to reduce waist circumference and sculpt the abdomen and flanks.
card.note: Clinic-administered device; most published studies are small and company-linked.

quick.overview:
Liposonix was a clinic-based body-contouring system that uses high-intensity focused ultrasound to destroy fat cells in a targeted layer below the skin. It is aimed at the abdomen and flanks, where treated patients are reported to lose waist circumference after a single session.

Published work includes a three-study safety programme in 152 volunteers, a retrospective case series of 85 patients, a porcine study and a review of the technology.
quick.how: A clinician applies the handpiece to marked areas and delivers focused energy at a set depth below the skin, in a session lasting about 1 to 1.5 hours in one case series. The body then clears the disrupted fat gradually through its inflammatory response.
quick.risks: Safety studies reported the ultrasound effect remained within the targeted fat layer. Heating-based fat devices can have side effects such as discomfort and bruising, and a separate report describes paradoxical fat growth after a radiofrequency treatment. Treatment should be done by a trained professional.

lead: Liposonix is a non-surgical body-contouring system that uses high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) to disrupt fat cells percutaneously.[1] The energy crosses the skin at low intensity and is focused at a point in the subcutaneous fat, where it raises temperature and kills fat cells while sparing the skin surface.[1][2]

People use it for appearance purposes: reducing waist circumference and localized abdominal or flank fat without surgery.[2] In a retrospective chart review of 85 men and women with a mean age of 43.8 years, a single session of 1 to 1.5 hours at a focal depth of 1.1 to 1.6 cm was associated with reduced waist circumference.[2]

Earlier work includes a porcine preclinical study[3] and a three-study programme evaluating safety in 152 healthy volunteers across total energy doses of 47 to 331 J/cm2, including patients treated before elective abdominoplasty so tissue could be examined.[4]

chain: Focused ultrasound aimed at subcutaneous fat
angle.text: The device removes fat volume from a targeted area, which changes waist and flank contour; reports describe measurable waist-circumference reductions after one session.

infobox: Medicis Technologies Corporation (as named in studies)

paras: The beam is focused at a depth below the epidermis, so the skin receives low intensity while the focal zone heats fat. Disrupted fat cells attract macrophages, which carry away lipids and debris, reducing local fat volume.[1] Another paper describes the same process as instantaneous cell death through coagulative necrosis within the targeted area.[2]

In the 152-patient safety programme, post-treatment ultrasound confirmed that effects stayed within the targeted fat layers, and evaluation included blood chemistry, haematology, examinations and adverse events.[4]

A 2010 retrospective case series covered 85 patients treated at one clinic.[2] A 2011 clinical study reported on 152 volunteers in three safety studies,[4] and a 2011 paper described preclinical work in pigs.[3] A 2009 review described clinical and histological findings.[1]

timeline.event: Review describes HIFU fat disruption with Liposonix.[1]
Retrospective case series of waist-circumference reduction published.[2]
Human safety studies and porcine study published.[3][4]
